messages:
maya: Quick flag — I'm seeing a keyboard focus trap in the suppression timepicker inside the Alert edit modal. Repro: open alert -> Edit suppressions -> tab through controls -> focus gets stuck in the timepicker. david: Hmm, can repro on mac + Chrome. Looks like the timepicker's internal list captures focus. Could be the datepicker lib's focusOnMount behavior. elena: Agree this is a big a11y blocker. Two quick UX options: 1) replace with segmented numeric inputs (H:mm) + incremental arrows so keyboard flows naturally, 2) keep timepicker but add an explicit close/tab index hack. I prefer option 1 for predictability. maya: Here's a quick Figma mock: https://figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/suppress-segmented — shows segmented hours / minutes and an "Apply to channel" toggle visible in-panel. Also added helper text under the input. sam: Small copy thought: we currently show "Quiet period" on the rule. Users have confused that with mute in support. Might be clearer as "Snooze window" or "Silence for". Not sure about terminology parity with current docs. elena: I reviewed the copy guide — "Silence" is used elsewhere for user-level muting. "Snooze window" reads friendlier but could imply one-off. I vote for "Silence for" (verb + duration) in the inline label and keep the rule card title as "Quiet period" for visibility. designbot: Automated accessibility check results for thread 2198765432: 1) preview list missing aria-describedby linking to helper text; 2) suppressed-channel badge contrast < 4.5:1 on dark theme; 3) timepicker traps keyboard focus (WCAG 2.1.2). Please address before shipping. david: For the preview pane — it also doesn't reflect channel priority ordering when multiple channels are selected. The mock shows a simple list but our backend routing adds priorities which users expect to see. Need to add a small chevron/ordering indicator. maya: Good point. I added a tiny badge showing "#1 / #2" next to each channel in the mock. It uses an aria-label: "Channel priority {{n}} of {{total}}" so screenreader users get ordering context. elena: Implementation note — add aria-describedby to the preview container and referencing an offscreen help node id="preview-help" with text: "Preview shows channel order and what notifications look like. If a channel is muted by policy it will show a muted badge." david: Pseudocode for aria helper insertion: ```html
  • #email - email@example.com
Preview shows final notify order and badges (muted, snoozed).
``` sam: Another front-end nit: the muted badge color fails contrast on dark theme — I can propose accessible hex values. Also maybe replace color-only state with an icon + text for clarity. maya: Action items: 1) I'll update Figma to segmented inputs + priority badges + copy change suggestion and push new frames (due EOD). 2) @david will add e2e keyboard-nav test covering tab order and ensure timepicker doesn't trap (I'll attach test plan). 3) @elena will add aria-describedby and microcopy for preview (linking to docs). 4) @sam will provide accessible badge color tokens and fallback iconography suggestions. david: I'll also add a unit test that the preview list DOM includes aria-describedby and that focus moves out of the suppression panel when tabbing forward. elena: Minor follow-up: for the severity slider we should add aria-valuetext like "Severity: critical" for SR users. I'll add to the same PR. maya: Thanks all. I'll open a short PR with the markup changes once Figma is updated and ping designbot for a re-run of the axe checks. :thumbsup:
